text:
alex: quick heads-up — ran an A/B microbatch sweep on kv-compact + kernel-selector. results look weird: prefill p95 dropped but decode p99 regressed.
priya: can you paste the breakdown numbers? also which model variant and seq-len distribution?
alex: model=redwood-7b-open, seqs: 75% short (<=64), 25% long (<=512). batch windows: 8/16/32 microbatch sizes. summary:

alex: ```
A (baseline): prefill p95=45ms, decode p95=60ms, decode p99=210ms
B (kv-compact + new_kernel): prefill p95=30ms, decode p95=80ms, decode p99=320ms
``` 
alex: so we shaved prefill but tail decode latency spikes. raw traces attached to repo link (see bench-bot). :eyes:
bench-bot: http://ci/bench/1847654321 — full flamegraphs + per-core timelines
jamie: interesting. do the p99 spikes correlate with KV cache misses or kernel fallbacks?
marta: my guess: kernel-selector is choosing a quantized path that has worse decode latency for long sequences due to suboptimal attention kernel for cached KV shapes.
priya: can you share a small log excerpt showing kernel decisions for a slow trace?

alex: pasted below one slow request trace:

alex: ```
TRACE slow_req:
  prefill: 28ms (kernel=fast_prefill)
  decode step 1..5: 12ms each (kernel=fast_decode)
  decode step 6: 140ms (kernel=slow_matmul_fallback)
  decode step 7..end: 15ms each
  kv_cache: hit ratio=0.67
```

jamie: that sudden fallback at step 6 smells like a kernel shape mismatch — maybe we switched from 16->32 key dims after microbatching boundary? could be batching splitter rounding.
marta: also check our kernel warmup: some quantized kernels take non-trivial setup on first use, then amortize. did you run with cold-start disabled?
alex: cold-start was disabled but we did spin up new worker nodes for B. warmup might still be noisy.
priya: if it's a one-off kernel init, p99 shouldn't be that high across multiple traces. are the slow spikes aligned with long sequences only?
alex: yes mostly long ones, but not exclusively. a couple short ones hit it too.
jamie: next steps proposal:
  - instrument kernel-selector to log chosen kernel + fallback reason (shape/precision/other)
  - add microsecond-resolution timeline annotation for KV cache misses vs kernel init
  - run targeted replay of slow traces with profiler sampling at 1ms
priya: +1. also try forcing kernel pinning (force old_kernel) on B to confirm delta. if decode tail disappears we know selector is the cause.
marta: can we experiment with splitpoint adjustments? make prefill larger so decode sees warmer KV cache and more consistent shapes.
ops-bot: reminder — canary cluster has 20% traffic cap, extended 2h for diagnostic runs. :lock:
alex: i'll run the forced-pin replay and add the selector logs. will also re-run with splitpoint +1 token to see warmup effects.
jamie: if you need quick kernel rollback, I can roll back selector change and patch rollout policy.

alex: thanks — i'll drop results in this thread and tag everyone. short-term priority: remove decode p99 regressions even if we lose a little prefill gain. long-term: make kernel selection cost-aware for tail latency.
priya: agree. cost-aware + shape-prediction heuristics could avoid these mid-decode fallbacks.

marta: one more note — add a metric for "kernel-init-ms per-request" to Console so we can alert on sudden increases.
alex: added to backlog: PERF-1287. creating a mini playbook for reproducing this locally.

alex: update: ran forced-pin -> decode p99 returned to 220ms, prefill p95 back to 45ms. looks like selector is causing the tail.
priya: excellent repro. can you attach selector log snippet and assign to eng-runtime? i'll triage priority.
alex: attaching logs and assigning ENG-460. end of thread for now. :thumbsup:
